newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shekel tumbles 1.5 pct against dollar.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shekel tumbles 1.5 pct against dollar.

text.p: The Israeli shekel tumbled 1.5 percent against the dollar to 3.58 shekels on Thursday, as the decline that began at the end of last week picked up pace, traders said.
The spreads reported by banks ranged from 3.57/3.58 shekels per dollar to 3.58/3.60.
"It's a nervous market," said a trader at Bank Hapoalim. "The shekel could break 3.60 unless the (Bank of Israel) governor intervenes. Intervention would calm a very nervous market."

The shekel has fallen by 4.7 percent since last Friday, shortly after the government announced a reform of the exchange rate regime and the Bank of Israel lowered the base rate by a steep 1.2 percentage points to 12.7 percent.

"Trading was very volatile today. It's like a snowball and investors are afraid of getting stuck in the wrong position," said Zahi Elias of Bank Leumi. "The private sector is paying off foreign currency loans and investors are closing positions."
But a trader at First International Bank said speculators were driving the shekel down. "We want to see if it will drop to 3.60. I don't think it will," he said.
Dealers described Thursday's market as turbulent.

"After the representative rate was set on Wednesday the shekel fell to 3.57 shekels to the dollar and the trend continued into Thursday, with the dollar touching 3.6 shekels before the shekel started recovering," Elias said.
"Over the course of the day the dollar reached 3.6 shekels once more only to decline again," he said.
Elias said the decision of the central bank to ease certain foreign currency regulations prevented the shekel from declining further.
The Bank of Israel said on Thursday it had cancelled the one-month minimum term for a foreign currency-linked and inflation-linked deposits. It also eased forex liquidity requirements for the banks.

The representative rate for the dollar was fixed at 3.5800 shekels against 3.5240 on Wednesday. The basket, composed of the dollar, mark, pound sterling, French franc and yen, was fixed at 3.8946 against 3.8355 on Wednesday.
On the crosses, the shekel traded against the yen at 3.1481 shekels per 100 yen compared with 3.0933 on Wednesday, and against the mark at 2.0727 shekels compared with 2.0459 on Wednesday.
In late afternoon, the dollar was trading at 3.5730 shekels.
